newsitem.title: MEXICO: POLL- Alfa seen posting high Q2 cash flow.
newsitem.headline: POLL- Alfa seen posting high Q2 cash flow.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Alfa S.A. is seen posting record high cash flow in the second quarter, with growing revenues and increasing operating profits, analysts said.

But per share earnings are seen lower, affected much as they were in the first quarter when high revenues were not enough to offset a decline in real selling prices in pesos caused by a stronger peso and a reduction in international selling prices for some of its commodities.
A survey of four industry analysts found expectations of average earnings per share of 1.14 pesos during the second quarter, compared to 1.83 pesos during the same period of 1996.
They forecast average operating income of 1.24 billion pesos, compared to 1.23 in the second quarter of 1996.
The analysts predicted average revenues of 7.44 billion pesos in the second quarter, versus 7.376 billion pesos in the second quarter of 1996.

But where the company is really expected to shine is in the cash flow from its dollar earnings, which are seen hitting new records in the second quarter on the back of continued good domestic sales and exports.
"They have had steady growth on a dollar basis and we expect the same in the second quarter," said Alexis Panton, an analyst with Caspian Securities.

In the first quarter Alfa generated record high earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of $197 million, 9.0 percent above the $181 million in the fourth quarter of last year.
The company Robert Fleming is forecasting that EBITDA will reach $210 million in the second quarter.
Valores Finamex has raised its EBITDA target to $211 million from an earlier forecast $203 million.
"All divisions are expected to report very impressive results," wrote Valores Finamex analyst Angeli Hemm.
Alfa, one of Mexico's biggest companies, has five divisons made up of steel (Hylsamex), petrochemicals (Alpek), food (Sigma), telecommunications (Onexa) and retail and auto parts (Versax).
